intro: **IIFYM (If It Fits Your Macros)** — also called *flexible dieting* — lets you track macros without banning any food: as long as it fits your daily numbers, you can eat it. Pioneered by Layne Norton, PhD, it operates on [caloric deficit](/calculadora-deficit-calorico-perder-peso-semana) and sufficient protein. The standard split is **30% protein / 30% fat / 40% carbs** for body recomposition. The **80/20 rule** means 80% of your intake should be nutrient-dense (lean protein, vegetables, whole grains) and up to 20% can be flexible (pizza, ice cream, chocolate). Enter your daily calorie target and this calculator delivers your exact macro targets in seconds.
keyTakeaway: IIFYM: **30% protein + 30% fat + 40% carbs**. 80/20 rule: nutritious/flexible. If it fits, eat it.

example.title: Example: 2,500 kcal IIFYM breakdown
steps: **Protein**: `2,500 × 0.30 ÷ 4 kcal/g` = **188 g** (≈ 12 oz chicken breast + 2 eggs).
**Fat**: `2,500 × 0.30 ÷ 9 kcal/g` = **83 g** (≈ 2 tbsp olive oil + 1 avocado + handful of almonds).
**Carbs**: `2,500 × 0.40 ÷ 4 kcal/g` = **250 g** (≈ 2 cups cooked rice + 2 medium fruits).
**Flexible 20%**: `2,500 × 0.20` = **500 kcal** (1 slice pizza + small ice cream, or 2 beers).

explanation:
## What is IIFYM?

**If It Fits Your Macros**. The principle is simple: body weight is determined by caloric balance; body composition (muscle vs fat) is determined by macro distribution — primarily protein. Popularized by Layne Norton, PhD in nutritional physiology, IIFYM is now one of the most evidence-based flexible dieting frameworks.

## IIFYM macro reference table

| Daily Calories | Protein (g) | Fat (g) | Carbs (g) | Flex (kcal) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,500 kcal | 113 g | 50 g | 150 g | 300 kcal |
| 1,800 kcal | 135 g | 60 g | 180 g | 360 kcal |
| 2,000 kcal | 150 g | 67 g | 200 g | 400 kcal |
| 2,200 kcal | 165 g | 73 g | 220 g | 440 kcal |
| 2,500 kcal | 188 g | 83 g | 250 g | 500 kcal |
| 3,000 kcal | 225 g | 100 g | 300 g | 600 kcal |
| 3,500 kcal | 263 g | 117 g | 350 g | 700 kcal |

*Standard distribution: 30% protein / 30% fat / 40% carbs.*

## Standard macro split

| Macro | % Calories | Conversion | 2,500 kcal example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Protein | 30% | ÷ 4 kcal/g | 188 g |
| Fat | 30% | ÷ 9 kcal/g | 83 g |
| Carbohydrates | 40% | ÷ 4 kcal/g | 250 g |

## The 80/20 rule

- **80% nutrient-dense**: vegetables, fruits, whole grains, lean protein, legumes, low-fat dairy.
- **20% flexible**: whatever you enjoy — pizza, dessert, alcohol — as long as macros close for the day.

With 2,000 kcal, 400 kcal flexible = a large ice cream or a generous slice of pizza.

## Macro adjustment by goal

| Goal | Protein | Fat | Carbs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Muscle gain (bulk) | 25% | 25% | 50% |
| Body recomposition | 30% | 30% | 40% |
| Fat loss (cut) | 35–40% | 25–30% | 30–35% |

## Pros and limitations

**Pros**: high adherence, social-life friendly, science-backed (caloric deficit + protein), no food groups banned.

**Limitations**: requires a food scale and tracking app, micronutrients can be neglected without the 80/20 rule, initial learning curve.

## Related calculators

- [Protein per meal calculator](/calculadora-proteina-por-comida-anabolismo) — distribute daily protein optimally.
- [Daily fiber calculator](/calculadora-fibra-diaria-edad-sexo) — ensure the 80% nutritious portion covers fiber needs.
- [Caloric deficit calculator](/calculadora-deficit-calorico-perder-peso-semana) — calculate your calorie target first.

faq.a: **If It Fits Your Macros**. A flexible dieting approach where you track protein, fat, and carbohydrates rather than restricting specific foods. If the food fits your daily macro targets, you can eat it — no guilt.

faq.q: What is the standard IIFYM macro split?
faq.a: The most common IIFYM split is **30% protein, 30% fat, 40% carbs**. For 2,000 kcal: 150 g protein, 67 g fat, 200 g carbs. For a fat-loss phase, protein is often raised to 35–40%; for a bulk, carbs go up to 50%.

faq.q: Can I eat pizza or ice cream on IIFYM?
faq.a: Yes — within the 80/20 rule. **20% of daily calories can be flexible**. On 2,000 kcal that's 400 kcal for treats (one generous slice of pizza or a large ice cream). The remaining 80% (1,600 kcal) should come from nutrient-dense whole foods.

faq.q: How many grams of protein do I need on IIFYM?
faq.a: At 30%: **protein (g) = daily calories × 0.30 ÷ 4**. Examples: 1,800 kcal → 135 g; 2,500 kcal → 188 g; 3,000 kcal → 225 g. During a cut, raising protein to 35–40% better preserves lean mass.

faq.q: Is IIFYM effective for weight loss?
faq.a: Yes — the mechanism is **caloric deficit**. IIFYM doesn't change energy physics: eat less than you burn and you lose weight. Its advantage is adherence: no forbidden foods means you stick to it for months instead of weeks. A typical deficit is 300–500 kcal/day.

faq.q: What's the difference between IIFYM and regular calorie counting?
faq.a: Calorie counting controls total energy; IIFYM controls **each macro separately**. Two 2,000-kcal diets can produce very different body composition outcomes depending on their protein content. IIFYM ensures adequate protein for muscle retention.

faq.q: What apps are best for IIFYM macro tracking?
faq.a: Top options: **MyFitnessPal** (largest food database, free tier available), **MacroFactor** (auto-adjusts TDEE over time), **Cronometer** (detailed micronutrient tracking), **Carb Manager** (low-carb focused). All scan barcodes.

faq.q: Do I need to track micronutrients on IIFYM?
faq.a: Not strictly required, but recommended. The 80/20 rule naturally covers most micronutrients. Watch out for **vitamin D, iron, and zinc** if your diet is low in animal products or sun exposure is limited.

Yes, but expect a 2–3 week learning curve. The most important tool: **a digital kitchen scale** — eyeballing food introduces 20–30% errors that kill results. Use an app like MyFitnessPal until you know the macro values of your staple foods.

faq.q: How accurate do I need to be with macro tracking?
faq.a: Within **±5–10 g per macro per day** is excellent. Perfect accuracy isn't realistic or necessary. What matters is consistent tracking over weeks — a day off by 15 g protein won't derail progress, but systematic under-tracking by 300 kcal/day will.

referenceTables.note: Source: Atwater general factor system (Wilbur O. Atwater) — the standard energy values used on nutrition labels and by macro-tracking apps. Protein and carbohydrate yield 4 kcal/g, fat 9 kcal/g, alcohol 7 kcal/g, and most dietary fiber roughly 2 kcal/g. *Gram targets shown for the calculator's default 30/30/40 split on a 2,500 kcal day; the 'flexible' 20% (500 kcal) is where alcohol and treats fit.
referenceTables.caption: Fat packs 9 kcal/g — more than twice protein or carbs — and alcohol's 7 kcal/g is the macro most trackers forget to log.

referenceTables.title: Daily Protein Target by Goal (ISSN) — Sense-Check Your Macro Split
referenceTables.note: Source: International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN) Position Stand on Protein and Exercise (Jäger et al., 2017, JISSN; PMC5477153). The 0.8 g/kg RDA covers sedentary needs only, not training; endurance/general active needs run ~1.2–1.4 g/kg. For resistance exercisers, 1.4–2.0 g/kg/day supports building or maintaining muscle; ~1.6 g/kg is the commonly cited optimum with diminishing returns up to ~2.2 g/kg; during a calorie deficit, resistance-trained individuals may need 2.3–3.1 g/kg to retain lean mass. Use this to sanity-check the protein gram figure the calculator gives you: the IIFYM 30%-of-calories default lands near these targets at typical calorie levels, but very high-calorie bulks (low g/kg) or aggressive cuts (needing high g/kg) may justify nudging the protein % up.
referenceTables.caption: Cross-check the protein grams above against your bodyweight — ~1.6–2.2 g/kg for most, up to 3.1 g/kg when cutting to protect muscle.
